independent_check.summary: Written from scratch in this lane. Exact sympy: deleted-sum equals formal derivative; P'(z)=3(z-B+)(z-B-) as polynomial identity mod q^2-1-27/16 u^2; q^2=1+27/16 u^2 with |q^2| in [11/16,43/16] exactly (never 0, sup|q|=sqrt(43)/4<2); all six B=aj cases impossible exactly (force u=+-4/3 contradicting |u|=1, or |q|=2); fiber roots pairwise distinct (differences rho(1-su), rho(1+su), 2rsu all nonzero pointwise); endpoint distance exactly 3/5+3sqrt(43)/40 > 21/20. Plus 2001-point mpmath scan at 80 dps: max identity residual 1.7e-80, max weight residual 4.2e-81, min weight 2.92e-3, max root norm 0.9, max critical norm 0.79180788...

SOURCE: Exact statements of published Conjecture 3 (p60) and preprint Conjecture 2.5 match the proposed refutation target; hypotheses verified: n=3, a_j in D*(0,1) (strictly inside), p' admits exactly n-1=2 roots B± in D*(0,1), each writable per Equation (1) with strictly positive elements of A.
Published Conjecture 4 (fully split derivative, no convex-weight hypothesis) is also satisfied and refuted by the same example: P' completely factors as 3(z-B+)(z-B-).

FINDING (nuance, non-blocking): Definition 2 / 2.3 uses (z-a)(z-a)* <= sqrt(r)*1, not r*1; the text-layer extraction drops the radical. Immaterial at r=1 (both give the pointwise |z(t)-a(t)|<=1 condition), but the formalization must state the exact definition.

FINDING (non-blocking): the step 'P'(B)=0 and P(B) invertible => sum_j (B-aj)^{-1}=0' in PROOF.md uses commutativity of A (in a noncommutative algebra p(z)^{-1}p'(z) != sum (z-aj)^{-1} under factor reordering). Valid here since A=C([0,1],C) is commutative; recommend an explicit remark in formalization. The source's Theorem 1 is likewise stated only for commutative A, so there is no source gap.
MathDB 353909/353908 both open with zero solutions/comments/model attempts as of 2026-10-26 live fetch.
MATH: All identities exact (symbolic), all inequalities with strict rational/exact margin (43/16<4, 43/16>9/4, 3/5+3sqrt(43)/40>21/20, sqrt(43)/4<2).

Critical-point classification is complete and correct: any critical b gives continuous f=(3b/rho-1)/q with f^2=1 (q never 0), f constant on connected [0,1], so the only critical elements are B+ and B-. Connectedness is essential: in a disconnected base, pointwise mixing would create extra critical elements; C([0,1],C) having zero divisors is precisely why the algebraic argument alone is insufficient and the topological step is required.

Convex weights: each B-aj is nowhere zero (exact case analysis), hence invertible; P'(B)=P(B)*sum_j (B-aj)^{-1} in the commutative algebra gives sum (B-aj)^{-1}=0; conjugating gives sum r_j(B-aj)=0 with r_j=|B-aj|^{-2}>0, so B=sum omega_j a_j, omega_j=r_j/sum r_i strictly positive continuous, sum=1. This is the source's own construction ((z-aj)(z-aj)*)^{-1} normalized, so it meets Equation (1) exactly.
Refutation margins: both critical elements have sup-distance exactly 3/5+3sqrt(43)/40 approx 1.0918 > 1 from a0; distance exceeds 1 at t=0 (B-) and t=1 (B+), so neither lies in D*(a0,1).

Classical scalar Sendov is NOT contradicted: each fiber polynomial P_t is a scalar cubic with all roots in |z|<=0.9; the per-fiber near critical point exists at every t but switches branch (B+ near a0 at t=0, B- near a0 at t=1); no single continuous element can follow it.
NOVELTY: No prior refutation of the C*-algebraic or commutative C*-algebraic Sendov conjecture found: MathDB live (0 solutions), OpenAlex citations (4, all self-citations of the source preprint), arXiv abs:Sendov sweep (37 entries, none operator-algebraic counterexamples), pubdb sendov tag (5 entries, none counterexamples), Krishna's follow-ups (2206.06653 Schoenberg degree-2, 2206.08154 Smale MVT degree-2) do not resolve or refute it.

No immediately subsuming negative result found on continuous selection / monodromy of critical points in the Sendov setting; the nearest literature (continuous selections of polynomial functions, arXiv 2007.03952) is unrelated to Sendov proximity.

The square-root branch-switching / monodromy mechanism is classical and receives no novelty credit (as PROOF.md already states); the new content is its instantiation as a full counterexample satisfying ALL source hypotheses including the complete derivative factorization and strictly positive continuous convex weights.
